summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square between Buildings 2 and 12 and Parcel D, the Building 12 entry plaza on 22nd Street, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. Building 12 itself reopened in 2022 and Maryland Street's paving is done, but the plaza is a Phase 1 park still tied to adjacent vertical development.

milestones.text: DDA terms approved: parks completed 12-18 months after adjacent buildings, with Port Commission schematic design approval

Building 15 lifted and moved from its temporary location to its permanent location over the newly built 22nd Street during Phase 1 infrastructure work (dated in the Port's deck only to the 2018-2020 'Phase 1 Infrastructure Completed' window)

Building 12 receives its temporary certificate of occupancy; the plaza area around it hosts interim activations (Paint the Void retrospective inside Building 12, roller rink under Building 15 in 2021)
Streets around Pier 70, including Maryland Street with specialty pavers and gingko trees, opened to the public
Building 12 Preview Party, a two-day community event with all Building 12 tenants

Port reports that although Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure and Building 12's rehabilitation are complete, construction of the balance of Phase 1, 'largely comprised of the Phase 1 parks and open space,' will be built 'on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development,' which 'has not moved forward' because of pandemic-driven office-vacancy increases, construction-cost escalation and higher financing costs

No completion date is sourced for the plaza: its Phase 1 park schedule is tied to adjacent vertical development, which has not moved forward. The only outer bound in the documents is the 2017 DDA's whole-project Phase 3 outside date (about 2042), shown here as a soft placeholder
milestones.basis_note: 2017 DDA Schedule of Performance outside date for Phase 3, the Project's final phase, approximately 25 years after the 2017 approval (about 2042) (Port Item 9B, Table A, p.7); soft: the DDA's outside dates are extended for down market delay, which Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) reports has tolled the developer's time-sensitive deadlines since June 2021 (60-month maximum reached June 2026, extended to Dec 26, 2026), and 11A proposes parcel-specific outside dates, shorter phase timelines and a five-year DDA term extension; no revised date for this parcel is sourced yet. It is not a forecast for this Phase 1 plaza; Port Item 11A proposes to better align open spaces with a revised vertical development schedule.

facts.value: 3.9 'Building 12 Plaza and Market Square', zone 5 of Figure 3.4.1

Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction on three sides, four access ways, a compact tree grove), Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd Street, Maryland Street Platform, and the Building 15 structural frame pending a structural feasibility study
A pedestrian opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D; the existing passageway through Buildings 2 and 12; a Building 12 entrance from 22nd Street; a direct entry from Maryland Street
Open-air markets, community gatherings, small performances; Market Square extends Maryland Street with coordinated paving to accommodate vendors and food trucks

Within the Phase 1 area (Port's 2026 Exhibit A); Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) lists Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) and Market Square (OS-2) among the Phase 1 parks, and Port Item 11A cites three acres of Phase 1 parks overall

open_questions: No Port Commission schematic design approval or construction record for Market Square or the entry plaza was found; the interim events documented by the Port took place inside Building 12 and under Building 15, not on a finished plaza.

Whether the Building 15 structural frame is being retained (the D4D marks it 'pending structural feasibility study'): the Port's June 2025 deck shows Building 15 relocated over 22nd Street but does not say what will remain of it.

No openly licensed or public-record post-rehabilitation photo of Building 12 was found (checked Wikimedia Commons -- geosearch, category and title search all came up empty for anything dated 2022 or later). Perkins&Will's Building 12 wayfinding photography (by Bruce Damonte, via DNCO's case study) and Pier 70's own project photography are copyrighted, but their press/media contacts may grant editorial, non-commercial clearance on request -- worth revisiting if someone follows up with them.
